'''St Johnstone Football Club''' is a [[professional sports|professional]] [[association football]] club in [[Perth, Scotland|Perth]], Scotland. The team competes in the {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}}, the top division of [[Scottish football league system|Scottish football]]. The club's name is derived from St John's Toun (or Saint Johnstoun)—an old name of Perth—and the team is nicknamed the "Saints". The club was officially founded in 1884, and the team played its first match in February 1885. Their home since 1989 has been [[McDiarmid Park]]; former home venues were the [[Recreation Grounds, Perth|Perth Recreation Grounds]] and, from 1924 to 1989, [[Muirton Park]]. The team's first [[Scottish Cup]] appearance was in [[1886–87 Scottish Cup|1886–87]] and they joined the [[Scottish Football League]] in [[1911–12 Scottish Division Two|1911–12]].

Historically, St Johnstone tended to float between the top two divisions of Scottish football and gained the reputation of being a "[[yo-yo club]]". The team won the [[Scottish Football League First Division]], then the second tier of Scottish league football, in [[2008–09 in Scottish football|2008–09]], bringing a return of first tier football to McDiarmid Park for the [[2009–10 in Scottish football|2009–10]] season after a seven-year absence. They played in the [[Scottish Premier League]], rebranded as the [[Scottish Premiership]] in 2013, for sixteen consecutive seasons, their longest ever stay in the highest league until relegation in 2025. St Johnstone's traditional rivals are the two [[Dundee]] clubs, [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] and [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], with matches between St Johnstone and either Dundee club being called "[[Tayside derby|Tayside derbies]]".

St Johnstone had limited success in cup competitions for the first 130 years of their history, losing at the semi-final stage on numerous occasions, as well as losing two [[Scottish League Cup]] finals. In [[2014 Scottish Cup final|2014]], they won their first [[Scottish Cup]] with a 2–0 win against Dundee United. In 2020–21, St Johnstone won their first League Cup and second Scottish Cup to complete a historic Cup double, becoming only the fourth team to achieve the feat. They defeated [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] 1–0 in the [[2021 Scottish League Cup final (February)|League Cup final]] and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] 1–0 in the [[2021 Scottish Cup final|Scottish Cup final]].

They have also won the [[List of winners of the Scottish Championship and predecessors|Scottish second tier]] eight times, the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] in [[2007 Scottish Challenge Cup final|2007]], the [[B Division Supplementary Cup]] in 1949 and the Scottish Consolation Cup in 1911 and 1914. They have qualified for [[UEFA competitions|European competitions]] in seven seasons, including four consecutively from [[2012-13 in Scottish football|2013]] to [[2015-16 in Scottish football|2016]]. Their highest league position in the [[List of Scottish football champions|top division]] is third place on three occasions: [[1970–71 Scottish First Division|1971]], [[1998–99 Scottish Premier League|1999]] and [[2012–13 Scottish Premier League|2013]]."}}
